turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also
satisfy a transparency requirement: the band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band
gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A selected candidate
whose band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I selected non-centrosymmetric selenides with light cations (Mg/Li/Ga) that are likely to retain band gaps ≥3 eV while having strong SHG from Ga–Se tetrahedral units. Heavy-metal selenides/tellurides and Cu/Ag/Tl/Hg compounds were deprioritized because their gaps are usually below 3 eV, despite sometimes large SHG. Among the remaining wide-gap selenides, denser and more Ga-rich Mg–Ga–Se phases are expected to have the largest |d_ij|.

Final: c032, c031, c001, c094, c014
